_about: Designed ElevenLabs voices (AUD-02), made by tools/voice/design_voices.py.

guard_2.description: A young man in his early twenties, a new recruit of the village watch. Clear, slightly nasal voice with a broad rural English accent, eager and a little nervous, trying to sound tougher than he is. Quick pace, close-mic, dry studio recording, no background noise.

guard_1.description: A man in his late thirties, a village watchman. Deep, steady, slightly gravelly voice with a rough northern English accent. Clipped, no-nonsense delivery, used to giving orders but not unkind. Speaks at a measured pace, close to the microphone, dry studio recording, no background noise.

villager_man_1.description: A warm, friendly middle-aged farmer, about forty-five. Mellow baritone voice with a soft rural West Country English accent, unhurried and good-humoured, with a smile in the voice. Close-mic, dry studio recording, no background noise.

villager_man_2.description: An older villager in his sixties, thin and a little reedy, with a dry, grumbling wit and a broad rural English accent. Speaks slowly and sighs a lot, the type who has seen everything twice. Close-mic, dry studio recording, no background noise.

villager_man_3.description: A big, broad-shouldered man in his early thirties, a gentle giant who works the fields. Deep, booming bass voice with a slow, easy rural English accent, warm and a little simple, quick to laugh. Close-mic, dry studio recording, no background noise.

villager_woman_1.description: A bright, lively young woman in her twenties, a farm worker. Light, warm mezzo voice with a gentle rural English accent, quick and cheerful with a teasing edge. Close-mic, dry studio recording, no background noise.

villager_woman_2.description: A capable woman in her fifties who runs a busy household. Firm, rich alto voice with a soft rural West Country English accent, practical and motherly, kind underneath the brisk manner. Close-mic, dry studio recording, no background noise.

villager_woman_3.description: An elderly woman in her seventies, the village's keeper of gossip and old stories. Thin, slightly cracked voice with a soft rural West Country English accent, sharp-witted and knowing, leaning in as if sharing a secret. Slow pace, close-mic, dry studio recording, no background noise.
